method_limits: the module name is a channel this study cannot close: any program can recover the card from the path without the producer's cooperation, so 'human-only' means 'human-only apart from the file name'

a docstring read is counted from three spellings only (ast.get_docstring, inspect/pydoc getdoc calls, and attribute reads of __doc__); a reader that shells out to a tool that prints docstrings is invisible here

the join tier requires a regex call whose argument is the docstring text or the variable it was assigned to; a join through a helper function or a two-step copy is not seen, so a zero join count is an upper bound on invisibility, not a proof of absence
sources with no signal are counted but not published row by row, so the tier tally and the row list do not have the same length (sources_scanned == rows + silent)
the docstring itself is never counted as a card literal site -- the study is about escaping it
population_source: every scripts/eNNN_*.py producer plus every .py source in the shared corpus (e432.corpus, self-excluded); producers are read for the three identity channels, all sources for docstring and card reads

probe.why: a pattern counts only when it hits its probe and misses both controls; an empty string or an empty alternation hits everything and is how the first cut published 1,203 'card-aware' sources
